data.narrative:
Cartesia is a Series B AI & Software company that has raised $186M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of nine private peers and one public reference (Palantir), spanning robotics, generative AI, and applied AI infrastructure at Series A through Series C stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a baseline proxy and applying a 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier, implies a valuation of $353M. Peer-median analysis across six same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $11.2B, with a range spanning $3.2B (Physical Intelligence, Series B) to $39.0B (Figure AI, Series C). The peer cohort reflects material heterogeneity in valuation outcomes even within the narrow AI & Software frontier-tech category.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $300M (low) to $12.8B (high), with a median point of $5.8B. The wide dispersion reflects structural uncertainty around how to weight stage-adjusted capital intensity against peer comparables that span materially different downstream applications and capital efficiency profiles. Stage-progression mechanics alone underweight the sector's valuation momentum relative to peers, while peer-median approaches may conflate companies at different functional maturity levels. Key uncertainties include Cartesia's revenue run-rate, unit economics relative to the peer set, and the sustainability of current AI software valuations in a normalizing capital environment.
